newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Kabila leaves Luanda, apparently for Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: Kabila leaves Luanda, apparently for Zaire talks.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila left Luanda on Saturday apparently to join an international peace summit on board a South African navy ship where President Mobutu Sese Seko is waiting for their first face-to-face talks, witnesses said.
"We believe Kabila has left Luanda and is on his way to meet Mobutu," a senior Western diplomat in Angola told Reuters. Witnesses said Kabila's plane departed at 9.40 a.m. (0840 GMT).
Kabila had arrived in the Angolan capital on Friday ahead of planned face-to-face peace talks with Mobutu, who he is fighting to overthrow, from the rebel stronghold of Lubumbashi in southeast Zaire.

But he pulled out of the talks late on Friday, demanding guarantees of his security and a say in the composition of an international peace summit before joining the negotiations on a South African naval vessel off the coast of West Africa.
South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, who was meant to escort Kabila to the SAS Outeniqua, had been due to return to Luanda on Saturday to brief Kabila about security measures on the ship.
But South African officials said he was still on board the ship, without giving further details.
